name: Mutton Kola Urundai
subtitle: deep-fried mince and lentil balls, dense and heavy with pepper and fennel

ingredients.note: lean; too much fat and the balls fall apart
the signature note of kola urundai
insurance if the mix is loose

prepNotes: Soak the chana dal 1 hour, then drain it thoroughly — wet dal makes a mix that will not hold its shape.
Boil the mince with turmeric and salt for 10 minutes and drain it well before grinding. Cooking first is what gives kola urundai its tight, dense bite.
Chill the ground mixture 20 minutes before rolling. Cold mix rolls smooth and does not crack in the oil.

steps.text: Boil the minced mutton with the turmeric, salt and 100ml water for 10 minutes, until it is cooked and dry. Drain and cool.
Dry-roast the pepper, fennel, cumin, chillies, cloves, cinnamon, star anise and stone flower for 3 minutes over low heat, then cool.
Grind the drained chana dal coarsely with the roasted spices — you want texture, not a paste.
steps.tip: Grind dry. Adding water here is the single most common reason kola urundai disintegrate in the oil.

steps.text: Add the cooked mince, shallots, garlic, ginger, curry leaves, coconut and coriander leaves and pulse to a thick, sticky mass.
Check the bind by rolling one ball. If it cracks or sags, work in the rice flour a spoon at a time. Chill 20 minutes.
Roll into smooth balls the size of a small lime, about 18 of them, pressing firmly.
Heat the oil to 170C — a pinch of the mix should rise in 3 seconds without browning instantly.
steps.tip: Too hot and the outside blackens while the middle stays raw-tasting; too cool and they soak up oil and break.

steps.text: Fry in batches of 5-6 for 5-6 minutes, turning, until deep mahogany brown and firm.
Drain on paper and rest 3 minutes before eating.

storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated. Reheat in a hot oven or dry pan for 5 minutes to crisp the shell; they can also be dropped into a kuzhambu and simmered 10 minutes.
